templates.name: monorepo/agents.md
templates.content:
# AGENTS.md

> Template: the project definition, the plan's rules, and the code's rules, for the root of a monorepo. Copy it to `AGENTS.md`, replace `acme` and every example value, and delete every line that starts with `>`. In a monorepo the planning session and every lane work in worktrees of this one repository, so all of them read this file. Keep it short, and put what holds for one package in that package's own `AGENTS.md`, with a `CLAUDE.md` beside it that imports it, which an agent reads once it works there.

This file defines the acme project and its rules for every agent that works in this repository: ropeshift's planning sessions, lanes, and reviews, and your own agent sessions. `CLAUDE.md` imports it.

## The project

> Two or three sentences: what the product is, who it serves, and the phase it is in.

acme lets customers manage their accounts and billing on their own. The plan of record is in `plan/`, and the current focus is in `docs/status.md`.

## Where things live

| Path | Holds |
|------|-------|
| `apps/api/`, `apps/web/` | The deployable applications, each with its own `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` |
| `packages/` | The libraries the applications share |
| `plan/` | The plan of record, in ropeshift's file format: the goal, plans, requirements, specs, architecture, experience designs, milestones, and contracts |
| `docs/decisions/` | Architecture decision records, `NNNN-short-title.md` |
| `docs/glossary.md`, `docs/status.md` | The project's terms, and the current focus |
| `scripts/` | The checks: `./scripts/check` and `./scripts/verify` |

## Commands

| Task | Command |
|------|---------|
| Install the dependencies | `make deps` |
| Quick check, before every commit | `./scripts/check` |
| Full verify, before the work is done | `./scripts/verify` |

## Which document wins

When two documents disagree, an accepted decision wins over a requirement, a requirement wins over a spec, an architecture document, or an experience design, and those win over notes and code comments. A contradiction is a question for a person: ask it, and never settle it by choosing one side.

## Writing plan files

- Plan files go under `plan/`: one file per document, milestone, or contract, named after its `id`, in lowercase with hyphens, ending in `.md`, starting with `+++` front matter that holds a known `kind`, a stable `id`, and a `title`. The `id` of a plan or a contract is a plain ID: 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, `-`, and `_`.
- This repository is the whole project, so it needs no manifest, and every work order changes it: leave `repo` out, or write `repo = "."`.
- Every contract belongs to a milestone, cites the documents it depends on, maps each criterion to requirement IDs, and has a criterion that `./scripts/verify` passes, mapped to `QA-1`.
- Say in a contract's statement which package its work changes, and cite code and evidence as `acme:apps/api/handler.go`.
- Requirements are `ACC-3`, an area code and a number, never reused. Never write a version number. Treat only accepted ADRs as binding.

## Rules for every change

- Use Conventional Commits, and keep each commit to one coherent change with its tests.
- Run `./scripts/check` before each commit and `./scripts/verify` before you report the work done, exactly as written, with no pipe or redirect, and report both results.
- Ask through the ask tool when the contract, its documents, and the decisions do not answer a question.
- Change `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `plan/`, `.ropeshift/`, `.claude/`, `.mcp.json`, and `scripts/` only when your contract asks for it.

## Privacy

Never commit a secret, a token, a local path, or a host name. Name a secret by reference, such as `env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

## Steps that need a person

Approving a plan, answering a question in Needs you, signing in with `eval "$(ropeshift login)"`, opening a run window for a subscription worker, merging at `person_merges`, and changing a repository setting or a policy are a member's steps.

templates.name: policies/solo/delegation-policy.toml
templates.content:
# The delegation policy: which permission requests of a lane the orchestrator may decide for you.
# Publish it as a member: ropeshift policy publish --file delegation-policy.toml
#
# The built-in version 1 delegates nothing, so every check a lane or a review runs waits for you. Set
# `version` to one more than the newest version `ropeshift policy list --kind delegation` prints.
[delegation_policy]
version = 2

# Each class names a tool and exactly one of command_prefix, path, or agent. A command matches when it
# is the prefix, or the prefix followed by a space and arguments, with no shell syntax such as a pipe,
# a redirect, or `&&`. A prefix admits any arguments, so name an entry point that takes none, such as a
# script, rather than `make` or `go test`, whose arguments can run something else.
#
# A check runs code the lane can change, as a commit hook does. A class trades your approval of each run
# for unattended progress, inside the limit of same-user isolation.

# The quick check, which a lane runs before each commit.
[[delegation_policy.classes]]
tool = "Bash"
command_prefix = "./scripts/check"

# The full verify, which a lane runs before it reports, and a review runs to judge the verify criterion.
[[delegation_policy.classes]]
tool = "Bash"
command_prefix = "./scripts/verify"

templates.name: policies/solo/notify-policy.toml
templates.content:
# The notify policy: where ropeshift tells you that something waits, beyond the web UI's Needs you.
# Publish it as a member: ropeshift policy publish --file notify-policy.toml
#
# The built-in version 1 sends nothing off the machine. Set `version` to one more than the newest
# version `ropeshift policy list --kind notify` prints.
[notify_policy]
version = 2
# A desktop notification on this machine, through osascript on macOS and notify-send on Linux. It
# carries the project's name and one fixed sentence, never a title, a question, or a path.
desktop = true

templates.name: policies/team/decision-policy.toml
templates.content:
# The decision policy: what an orchestrator may decide or assume on the question ladder, and what
# always reaches a person. Publish it as a member: ropeshift policy publish --file decision-policy.toml
#
# Every key must be stated, and a key the policy does not have is refused. Set `version` to one more
# than the newest version `ropeshift policy list --kind decision` prints; the built-in version is 1.
[decision_policy]
version = 2
# A reversible choice an orchestrator cannot answer from the plan becomes a recorded assumption, which a
# member can overturn later. "assume" is the only value.
reversible_default = "assume"
# Categories no orchestrator decides or assumes. A version must keep security, compliance, and data.
# A team adds business, so that pricing, terms, and commitments always reach a person.
one_way_categories = ["security", "compliance", "data", "business"]
# At most this many assumptions on one work order before its questions reach a person. The built-in
# value is 5. Fewer assumptions keep rework small when several people answer questions.
max_assumptions_per_work_order = 3

templates.name: policies/team/delegate-policy.toml
templates.content:
# The delegate policy: what the assistant and an outside delegate run with no confirmation card, and
# whether a delegate's lane start may raise the lane's model and effort. Publish it as a member:
# ropeshift policy publish --file delegate-policy.toml
#
# `version` and `exempt` must be stated. The built-in version 1 exempts nothing and allows a raise. The
# web UI's Settings shows the versions; `ropeshift policy list` does not take this kind.
[delegate_policy]
version = 2
# Consent operations a delegate runs with no card. Only four may be listed: work_order.accept,
# work_order.rework, work_order.create, and plan.start_review. A team lists none, so every one waits for
# a member's click.
exempt = []
# false holds a delegate's lane start to the model and effort its roster agent runs, so no agent raises
# the cost of shared work without a member.
raise_model_and_effort = false

templates.name: policies/team/delegation-policy.toml
templates.content:
# The delegation policy: which permission requests of a lane the orchestrator may decide for a member.
# Publish it as a member: ropeshift policy publish --file delegation-policy.toml
#
# The built-in version 1 delegates nothing. Set `version` to one more than the newest version
# `ropeshift policy list --kind delegation` prints.
[delegation_policy]
version = 2

# Each class names a tool and exactly one of command_prefix, path, or agent. A command matches when it
# is the prefix, or the prefix followed by a space and arguments, with no shell syntax. A prefix admits
# any arguments, so name entry points that take none. A team lists only entry points every repository of
# the project has, and leaves costly per-use agents with a member: it names no `agent` class.

[[delegation_policy.classes]]
tool = "Bash"
command_prefix = "./scripts/check"

[[delegation_policy.classes]]
tool = "Bash"
command_prefix = "./scripts/verify"

templates.name: policies/team/lane-policy.toml
templates.content:
# The lane policy: what a change under a running lane does to it. Publish it as a member:
# ropeshift policy publish --file lane-policy.toml
#
# Every key must be stated. Set `version` to one more than the newest version
# `ropeshift policy list --kind lane` prints; the built-in version is 1, which notifies on both.
[lane_policy]
version = 2
# A new version of the lane's contract or of a document it cites: "notify" tells the lane and lets it
# go on, and "park" also asks it to park until it is resumed.
on_contract_version = "notify"
# A one-way decision recorded while the lane runs, on the work it does. A team parks the lane, because
# work that goes on past a choice nobody can take back may have to be thrown away.
on_one_way_decision = "park"

templates.name: policies/team/notify-policy.toml
templates.content:
# The notify policy: where ropeshift tells members that something waits, beyond the web UI's Needs you.
# Publish it as a member: ropeshift policy publish --file notify-policy.toml
#
# Set `version` to one more than the newest version `ropeshift policy list --kind notify` prints; the
# built-in version 1 sends nothing off the machine.
[notify_policy]
version = 2
desktop = false
# An HTTPS address that receives each notice as JSON, such as a relay into the team's chat. It holds a
# host and a path only: a query or a user name in it is refused, because an address ends up in logs.
webhook_url = "https://hooks.example.com/ropeshift"
# The name of the variable in the daemon's environment that holds the signing key. It starts with
# ROPESHIFT_HOOK_, and the key itself never goes in a policy.
webhook_secret_env = "ROPESHIFT_HOOK_NOTIFY"

templates.name: pre-commit-config.yaml
templates.content:
# The pre-commit configuration, read by https://pre-commit.com/. Run `pre-commit install` once in each
# clone, and the hook below runs before every commit.
#
# One local hook runs the repository's quick check, scripts/check, and passes when the repository has none.
# Add the hooks of the tools the repository uses under `hooks`, or as further `repos`.
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: check
        name: scripts/check
        entry: sh -c 'if [ -x scripts/check ]; then exec scripts/check; fi'
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false
        always_run: true

templates.name: repository/agents.md
templates.content:
# AGENTS.md

> Template: the instructions for one code repository, for its root. Copy it to `AGENTS.md`, replace `acme-api` and every example value, and delete every line that starts with `>`. Ropeshift's lanes and reviews work in worktrees of this repository and read this file, never the workspace's, so every rule a change here must follow belongs in this file or in the contract.

This file gives coding agents, ropeshift lanes among them, what they need to change `acme-api`: what it is, its commands, its rules, and how a change is checked. `CLAUDE.md` imports it.

## What this repository is

`acme-api` is the HTTP API of the acme project. The project's plan of record, with its requirements, decisions, and contracts, lives in the `acme-workspace` repository, not here.

## Commands

> Name one entry point for each check, and make it take no arguments: ropeshift's delegation policy can then let the orchestrator approve exactly that command.

| Task | Command |
|------|---------|
| Install the dependencies | `make deps` |
| Quick check, before every commit | `./scripts/check` |
| Full verify, before the work is done | `./scripts/verify` |
| Run the service locally | `make run` |

## Layout

> The parts of the code an agent needs first: where the entry points, the domain, and the tests are.

- `cmd/api/`: the entry point.
- `internal/accounts/`: the accounts domain and its handlers.
- `internal/**/*_test.go`: the tests, beside the code they test.

## Rules

- Write the test that shows a behavior change before the change, and keep tests and code in one commit.
- Use Conventional Commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`. Keep each commit to one coherent change.
- When documents disagree, an accepted decision wins over a requirement, and a requirement over a spec or design. A contradiction is a question, never a choice.

## Working as a ropeshift lane

- Work only in your worktree, and commit on your own branch. Never push, and never move another branch.
- Run `./scripts/check` before each commit and `./scripts/verify` before you report the work done, exactly as written, with no pipe or redirect, and report both results with your outcome.
- Ask through the ask tool when the contract, its documents, and the decisions do not answer a question.
- Change `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.ropeshift/`, `.claude/`, `.mcp.json`, and the scripts under `scripts/` only when your contract asks for it, because they configure and check every later lane.
- Read other repositories only through the read-only trees your brief names.

## Privacy

This repository is public. Never copy text from the acme workspace's documents into code, comments, commit messages, or pull request text here, and never commit a secret, a token, a local path, or a host name.

templates.name: repository/catalog-info.yaml
templates.content:
# The components of this repository, in Backstage's descriptor format. Copy this file to catalog-info.yaml
# at the repository's root, or one per package folder, and commit it with the code it describes.
#
# ADR-0028 is accepted, and ropeshift reads this file from step C0 of the roadmap. Until then ropeshift
# ignores it. Backstage reads it as it stands, and the file must stay valid for Backstage, so every
# ropeshift field is an annotation under ropeshift.com/.
#
# Ropeshift will read every committed catalog-info.yaml on the repository's base branch, never the working
# tree, so an edit counts once it is merged. Each entity below is one component, and documents are
# separated by ---. A repository with no component here is one component named after the repository.
#
# Work orders name a component by its metadata.name: component = "acme-checkout".
---
apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component
metadata:
  # The purpose, first and required: one or two plain sentences on what the component is for and what it
  # owns. The planner, every lane and review of its work, the web UI, and the CLI read it, and work
  # naming a component with no description is not ready.
  description: >-
    Takes an order from cart to paid. Owns the checkout HTTP endpoints, the retry budget, and the
    idempotency keys sent to the payment provider.
  # The component's ID in the project, unique across every repository, and never changed: plan files,
  # decisions, and tracker mappings follow it. Letters, digits, and - _ . only, at most 63 characters.
  name: acme-checkout
  # The display name. Defaults to the name.
  title: Checkout
  # Plain labels. Ropeshift filters work and measures by them, and shows them to agents as text.
  tags:
    - payments
    - customer-facing
  # Key-value labels, such as the language or the service tier. Values follow the same rules as the
  # name, so quote numbers. Text for people and agents, never a rule.
  labels:
    language: go
    tier: "1"
  annotations:
    # Where the component lives, as path prefixes from the repository's root. Without it, a component
    # is the folder that holds this file, or the whole repository when the file is at the root. Paths
    # guide agents and review; they never limit what a lane may write.
    ropeshift.com/paths: services/checkout/, api/checkout/
    # What belongs here and what does not, one short item per line. The planner uses them to place
    # work, and the review reports a change that puts code where the component does not own it.
    ropeshift.com/owns: |
      Checkout endpoints and their request validation
      Retries and idempotency toward the payment provider
    ropeshift.com/does-not-own: |
      Prices and tax, which belong to acme-pricing
      The payment provider client, which belongs to acme-payments-client
    # Tracker identifiers. Jira uses the Jira plugin's keys; the adapter resolves the component name to
    # its Jira ID at the first sync, then maps by ID.
    jira/project-key: ACME
    jira/component: Checkout
    # The GitHub label exported issues carry for this component.
    ropeshift.com/github-component: "service:checkout"
    # When the component's code is in other repositories of the project, name them, comma-separated,
    # and write each path as <repository>:<prefix>. Without it, the repository is the one holding this
    # file, or the one backstage.io/source-location points to.
    # ropeshift.com/repositories: acme-api, acme-web
spec:
  # The kind: the word the team uses, such as service, website, library, app, package, or module. Free
  # text; ropeshift gives no kind any behavior.
  type: service
  # Required by Backstage. Shown to people and agents.
  lifecycle: production
  owner: group:acme-payments
  # Components this one builds on, by name. Ropeshift refuses a cycle across every repository's files,
  # lets a lane of this component read the repositories they live in, and shows what a change can affect.
  # They never order work orders; a contract's uses and depends_on do that.
  dependsOn:
    - component:acme-payments-client
---
apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component
metadata:
  description: >-
    The client the checkout service uses to call the payment provider. Owns the provider's request
    signing and its error mapping.
  name: acme-payments-client
  title: Payments client
  tags:
    - payments
  labels:
    language: go
  annotations:
    ropeshift.com/paths: libs/payments-client/
    ropeshift.com/github-component: "library:payments-client"
spec:
  type: library
  lifecycle: production
  owner: group:acme-payments

templates.name: repository/profile.toml
templates.content:
# This repository's layer of the lane profile. Copy it to .ropeshift/profile.toml at the root of the
# repository, and commit it with the code it configures.
#
# The worker reads it from this repository's clone on each machine, over the built-in layer and the
# person's own layer, profile.toml in the installation's state directory. It can narrow what a lane does
# and never widen it: it adds gates, lowers the lane caps and the permission mode, and cannot change
# push_on_stop, [agent.classes], or how the machine is measured. A key ropeshift does not know refuses
# the whole profile, and no lane of this repository starts, so keep to the keys below.
#
# The worktree root is a machine's choice, not a repository's: set it in each machine's own layer.

[agent]
# A gate makes one kind of action ask a person, in every permission mode. The gates of every layer join,
# so these add to the person's own. A lane already asks before every command except file edits, mkdir,
# rm, rmdir, mv, and git add, rm, mv, and commit in its worktree, so a gate matters for those actions.
#
# Gate every commit when this repository's commit hooks run files a lane can change, and you want a
# person to see each commit before its hooks run. Unattended lanes then wait at every commit.
# gates = ["Bash(git commit *)"]
#
# A gate on files, such as "Edit(.ropeshift/**)", asks only for those paths in a lane that runs in a
# terminal pane. Under such a gate a headless lane parks on every edit, whatever its path, so use one only
# where lanes run in panes. Write the path relative to the worktree, with no leading slash.

[review]
# How many times the review judges one work order before work it still fails waits for a person.
# The built-in bound is 3.
# max_review_rounds = 2

[admission]
# Fewer lanes of this repository at once, such as for a heavy build. It can only lower the person's cap.
# max_lanes = 2

[hooks]
# A command that runs once in a lane's new worktree, such as installing its dependencies. Each word is
# one argument, {lane.name} becomes the lane's name, and no shell reads it. It runs for at most ten
# minutes, and a failure stops the lane from starting.
# on_lane_created = ["make", "deps"]

templates.name: security.md
templates.content:
# Security policy

> Template: how to report a vulnerability, for `SECURITY.md` at the root of a repository, where the forge shows it. Copy it to `SECURITY.md`, replace `acme` and every example value, and delete every line that starts with `>`.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report a vulnerability in acme privately to security@acme.example, and do not open a public issue or pull request for it. Say which version is affected, how to reproduce the problem, and what an attacker gains.

## Supported versions

Only the latest release of acme receives security fixes.

templates.name: user/profile.toml
templates.content:
# Your own layer of the lane profile, for one machine. Copy it to profile.toml in the installation's state
# directory:
#
#   macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/ropeshift/profile.toml
#   Linux: $XDG_STATE_HOME/ropeshift/profile.toml, or ~/.local/state/ropeshift/profile.toml
#
# Only this layer sets the machine's lane caps, push_on_stop, and [agent.classes], and only it can widen
# what lanes do. A key ropeshift does not know refuses the whole profile and no lane starts, so keep to
# the keys below. The worker reads a change at its next start and its next measure.

[worktree]
# Every lane worktree of every repository goes under this root, outside the workspace and every clone,
# with each project's and repository's lanes apart: {project} becomes the project's ID and {repo} the name of the clone's folder. Write an absolute
# path, because the root expands no ~ and no variable. Choose a folder with no CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md in
# it or above it, because the agent CLI reads instruction files from every folder above its own. With no
# root set, the built-in root holds: the installation's worktree directory, by project and repository.
# root = "/path/to/lanes/{project}/{repo}"
# true pushes each lane's branch and checkpoint refs to the repository's remote when the lane stops, so
# its work survives the loss of this machine and a parked lane can resume on another. false keeps every
# lane's work on this machine until a merge or a pull request sends it. A worker that joined a group
# server ignores this key and always pushes.
push_on_stop = false

# The folder that holds a project's clones on this machine, by the project's ID. Ropeshift finds it by itself when the project's planning repository holds the other clones
# in a folder it ignores. Set it to name a folder that is not that clone, as an absolute path, or to ""
# to say the project has no workspace here. A lane worktree of a clone inside the workspace goes in the
# workspace's .ropeshift/worktrees/ folder, when the workspace's .gitignore ignores /.ropeshift/worktrees/.
# [projects.my-project-id]
# workspace = "/path/to/workspace"

[admission]
# The most lanes at once on one agent sign-in. Every lane on one subscription draws on its usage limits.
# 0 caps nothing.
max_lanes_per_sign_in = 3
# The most lanes at once on this machine. Unset, the worker's recommendation from the machine's cores and
# memory holds. Set it lower on a machine with no swap.
# max_lanes = 2

[telemetry]
# Keep the repository and branch out of lane telemetry, for repositories whose names must not leave this
# machine in an export.
# omit_repository = true

templates.name: workspace/agents.md
templates.content:
# AGENTS.md

> Template: the project definition and rules, for the root of the workspace repository. Copy it to `AGENTS.md`, replace `acme` and every example value, and delete every line that starts with `>`.

This file defines the acme project for every agent that works in this workspace: ropeshift's planning and adopt sessions, which run in worktrees of this repository, and your own agent sessions here. `CLAUDE.md` imports it. Each code repository has an `AGENTS.md` of its own for the agents that change it, because a lane works in a worktree of that repository and never reads this file.

## The project

> Two or three sentences: what the product is, who it serves, and the phase it is in.

acme lets customers manage their accounts and billing on their own. The plan of record is in `plan/`, and the current focus is in `docs/status.md`.

## Repositories

> The manifest is the record of the repositories. This table adds only what the manifest has no key for.

The manifest, `plan/repositories.md`, lists every repository of the project with its remote, its path under `repos/`, and its purpose, and `make setup` clones any that is missing. This repository, `acme-workspace`, is the planning repository and is not in the manifest.

| Repository | Visibility | Reviewed through |
|------------|------------|------------------|
| `acme-workspace` | Private | Plan approval |
| `acme-api` | Public | Pull requests |
| `acme-web` | Private | Pull requests |

## Where things live

| Path | Holds |
|------|-------|
| `plan/` | The plan of record, in ropeshift's file format: the goal, plans, requirements, specs, architecture, experience designs, milestones, contracts, and the manifest |
| `docs/decisions/` | Architecture decision records, one file each, `NNNN-short-title.md` |
| `docs/research/` | Research and evaluations, each fact with its source URL |
| `docs/glossary.md` | The project's terms |
| `docs/status.md` | The current focus |
| `repos/` | The code repositories, each a clone of its own, ignored by this repository |

## Which document wins

When two documents disagree, an accepted decision wins over a requirement, a requirement wins over a spec, an architecture document, or an experience design, and those win over notes and code comments. A contradiction is a question for a person: ask it, and never settle it by choosing one side.

## IDs

- Requirements: an area code and a number, such as `ACC-3`. An ID is never reused, even after its requirement is deleted.
- Decisions: `ADR-0007` for a record in `docs/decisions/`, and the ledger's own ID for a decision recorded through ropeshift.
- Milestones: `m1-accounts`. Contracts: the deliverable, such as `accounts-api`. Criteria: `c1`. Exit criteria: `e1`. Draft decisions: `d1`.
- Cite a document as `kind:id`, such as `spec:accounts-endpoints`, a requirement by its ID, and code as `repository:path`, such as `acme-api:internal/accounts/handler.go`.

## Writing plan files

- Plan files go under `plan/`: one file per document, milestone, or contract, named after its `id`, in lowercase with hyphens, ending in `.md`.
- Every plan file starts with a `+++` line, holds TOML front matter with a known `kind`, a stable `id`, and a `title`, and ends its front matter with another `+++` line. The `id` of a plan or a contract is a plain ID: 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, `-`, and `_`.
- Every contract belongs to a milestone, cites the documents it depends on in `documents`, and maps each criterion to requirement IDs.
- Every contract has a criterion that the full verify of the repository it changes passes, mapped to `QA-1`.
- Every work order names its repository in `repo`, by its name in the manifest. An absent `repo` is this workspace.
- A contract whose lanes must read this workspace's own prose, such as an ADR or the glossary, names `acme-workspace` in `reads`. A contract for a public repository does so only when its lanes need it.
- Never write a version number. Ropeshift numbers every committed change.
- Treat only accepted ADRs as binding.

## Conventions

- Write in English, in a plain engineering tone.
- Use Conventional Commits: `docs:`, `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`. Keep each commit to one coherent change.
- Use lowercase, hyphenated file names, except `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `CLAUDE.md`.

## Privacy

- This repository is private. Nothing from `plan/` or `docs/` goes into a public repository's code, comments, commit messages, or pull requests unless a person checked it first.
- Never commit a secret, a token, a local path, or a host name. Name a secret by reference, such as `env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

## Steps that need a person

| Step | How |
|------|-----|
| Approving a plan | `ropeshift plan approve`, or Needs you |
| Answering a question that reached Needs you | `ropeshift question answer`, or Needs you |
| Signing in | `eval "$(ropeshift login)"` in a terminal, for one hour |
| Registering repositories | `make register`, which asks for the passphrase |
| Opening a run window for a subscription worker | `ropeshift worker window-open <worker>` |
| Merging at `person_merges` | On the forge, or `git merge` of the lane's branch |
| Changing a repository's settings or a policy | `ropeshift repository set`, `ropeshift policy publish` |

## Working with ropeshift

- A planning session writes plan files on its own branch of this repository. Write nothing outside `plan/` and `docs/` there.
- Never edit ropeshift's state, and never ask a person for their passphrase. An agent outside ropeshift acts through a delegate credential a member made, and a consent action it prepares waits for the member's confirmation.
- `ropeshift needs` lists what waits for a person, and `ropeshift view roadmap` shows each milestone's progress. Read them instead of keeping that state in a file.

templates.name: workspace/makefile
templates.content:
# The workspace Makefile: clone, fetch, and show the status of every repository of the project, and run
# the ropeshift steps a person takes from here. Copy it to Makefile at the root of the workspace.
#
# Ropeshift never runs this file, and it clones nothing itself. It reads the manifest,
# plan/repositories.md. Keep REPOSITORIES in step with the manifest: the same names, remotes, and paths.

# The ropeshift project these repositories belong to. Create it once: ropeshift project create acme
PROJECT := acme

# The folder the code repositories are cloned into. The workspace's .gitignore ignores it.
CODE_DIR := repos

# Each code repository as name=remote, or name= when it has no remote. Its clone goes to $(CODE_DIR)/name, or to
# the path after a second =, relative to this folder: name=remote=path.
REPOSITORIES := \
  acme-api=git@github.com:acme/acme-api.git \
  acme-web=git@github.com:acme/acme-web.git

WORKSPACE := $(notdir $(CURDIR))

# ENTRY sets name, remote, and dir, the clone's folder, from the entry of REPOSITORIES a recipe loops over.
define ENTRY
name=$${entry%%=*}; rest=$${entry#*=}; remote=$${rest%%=*}; dir=$(CODE_DIR)/$$name; case "$$rest" in *=*) dir=$${rest#*=};; esac
endef

.PHONY: help setup fetch status hooks register-check register lanes

help:
	@echo 'make setup           clone each missing repository into $(CODE_DIR)/'
	@echo 'make fetch           fetch the workspace and every repository'
	@echo 'make status          show the branch and the changed files of every repository'
	@echo 'make hooks           install a pre-commit hook that runs the quick check of each repository'
	@echo 'make register-check  show what registering the repositories with ropeshift would do'
	@echo 'make register        register every repository, and name this one the planning repository'
	@echo 'make lanes           list merged lane branches and checkpoint refs, deleting nothing'

# Clone each repository that has no clone yet. A registered repository with no clone holds its work on
# this machine as no_checkout, so a fresh machine runs this before anything else.
setup:
	@mkdir -p $(CODE_DIR)
	@for entry in $(REPOSITORIES); do \
	  $(ENTRY); \
	  if [ -e "$$dir/.git" ]; then echo "$$name: present"; \
	  elif [ -z "$$remote" ]; then echo "$$name: no remote and no clone"; exit 1; \
	  else mkdir -p "$$(dirname "$$dir")" && git clone "$$remote" "$$dir" || exit 1; fi; \
	done
	@git check-ignore -q "$(CODE_DIR)/x" || echo "warning: .gitignore does not ignore $(CODE_DIR)/"
	@git check-ignore -q ".ropeshift/worktrees/" || echo "warning: .gitignore does not ignore .ropeshift/worktrees/, so lanes of these repositories run outside the workspace; add /.ropeshift/worktrees/"

fetch:
	@if [ -n "$$(git remote)" ]; then git fetch --all --prune --quiet && echo "$(WORKSPACE): fetched"; \
	else echo "$(WORKSPACE): no remote"; fi
	@for entry in $(REPOSITORIES); do \
	  $(ENTRY); \
	  if [ ! -e "$$dir/.git" ]; then echo "$$name: missing, run make setup"; \
	  elif git -C "$$dir" fetch --all --prune --quiet; then echo "$$name: fetched"; \
	  else echo "$$name: fetch failed"; fi; \
	done

status:
	@for entry in . $(REPOSITORIES); do \
	  if [ "$$entry" = . ]; then dir=.; name=$(WORKSPACE); else $(ENTRY); fi; \
	  label=$$name; \
	  if [ ! -e "$$dir/.git" ]; then echo "$$label: missing"; continue; fi; \
	  head=$$(git -C "$$dir" status --short --branch | head -n 1); \
	  changed=$$(git -C "$$dir" status --porcelain | wc -l | tr -d ' '); \
	  echo "$$label: $$head, $$changed changed"; \
	done

# Optional, for a project with no CI. Each clone gets a pre-commit hook in its own .git/hooks that runs
# scripts/check. Lane worktrees use their clone's hooks, so every lane commit runs the quick check, and a
# lane cannot edit the hook, which sits outside its worktree. Ropeshift's own merges and pushes run no hook.
hooks:
	@for entry in $(REPOSITORIES); do \
	  $(ENTRY); \
	  if [ ! -x "$$dir/scripts/check" ]; then echo "$$name: no scripts/check, skipped"; continue; fi; \
	  if [ -n "$$(git -C "$$dir" config core.hooksPath)" ]; then echo "$$name: core.hooksPath is set, skipped"; continue; fi; \
	  hook=$$(git -C "$$dir" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)/hooks/pre-commit; \
	  if [ -e "$$hook" ]; then echo "$$name: a pre-commit hook exists, kept"; continue; fi; \
	  printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec ./scripts/check\n' > "$$hook" && chmod +x "$$hook" && echo "$$name: installed"; \
	done

# Registration needs a member's session, so ropeshift asks for the passphrase on the terminal. The
# workspace needs at least one commit first, because a repository's identity is read from its history.
register-check:
	ropeshift repository add . $(CODE_DIR) --project $(PROJECT) --dry-run

register:
	ropeshift repository add . $(CODE_DIR) --project $(PROJECT)
	ropeshift repository set $(WORKSPACE) --planning --project $(PROJECT)

# Ropeshift never deletes a branch. After ropeshift lane archive <lane>, delete a merged branch with
# git branch -d lane/<lane>, and a checkpoint ref you no longer need with git update-ref -d <ref>.
lanes:
	@for entry in . $(REPOSITORIES); do \
	  if [ "$$entry" = . ]; then dir=.; else $(ENTRY); fi; \
	  if [ ! -e "$$dir/.git" ]; then continue; fi; \
	  base=$$(git -C "$$dir" symbolic-ref --quiet --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main); \
	  echo "$$dir, merged into $$base:"; \
	  git -C "$$dir" branch --list 'lane/*' --merged "$$base" --format='  %(refname:short)' 2>/dev/null; \
	  git -C "$$dir" for-each-ref --format='  %(refname)' refs/ropeshift/; \
	done
